subject: Access controls and support access — post-call recap

Subject: Access controls and support access — post-call recap

Hi Alice,

Thanks for taking time today — good conversation. Quick recap and a few follow-ups so we can scope the technical deep-dive: 

Summary of what we covered:
- Your primary concerns: PII handling, least-privilege RBAC, support access approval/auditability, and break-glass procedures.
- Data residency requirement: US-only (you mentioned production customer data must remain in US regions).
- Audit/log retention: you prefer >=12 months for support and admin activity logs.

Open questions we promised to confirm:
1) RBAC model: Do you need role-level separation down to per-environment (prod/stage) or is tenant-level roles sufficient?
2) Break-glass: Do you require multi-approver (2+ approvers) for emergency access, or is a single engineering manager + automatic audit acceptable?
3) Support access: Would you prefer ephemeral just-in-time admin sessions or a dedicated support service account with limited privileges?
4) Evidence: Which artifacts would be most helpful — SOC 2 mapping, example audit log extract, or a short runbook of the support access workflow?

Next steps I propose:
- I’ll send the access-controls overview and SOC 2 controls mapping (attached).
- Rishi (cc’d) will note how break-glass and support access are implemented from a security controls perspective.
- If that looks good, we’ll schedule a 60-min technical deep-dive with your engineering/security team + our solutions engineer (Monica) and Rishi.

Attaching: redwood_access_controls_overview.pdf (high-level; includes RBAC, support access flow, and break-glass summary).

Would you be available for a deep-dive next week (Mon/Tue preferred)?

Thanks,

—Marissa

Subject: Re: Access controls and support access — post-call recap

Hi Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. A few answers and a couple of asks from our security team: 

Answers:
- RBAC: We need tenant-level roles + environment separation. In practice that means distinct prod vs staging permissions; prod must be strictly scoped.
- Break-glass: We require 2 approvers for any emergency elevation to production (one must be a security approver).
- Support access: Prefer ephemeral, just-in-time admin sessions triggered via a ticket, but if there is a need for a support service account it must be constrained and require explicit approval per incident.
- Data residency: Confirmed — US-only.
- Audit retention: Minimum 12 months; longer is a plus.

Asks:
1) Can you provide SOC 2 controls mapping for access controls and support access?
2) Could you share an example audit-log extract (redacted) that shows a support access session and break-glass event?
3) Any details on how keys are handled for customer data (KMS/HSM)?

If you can share those artifacts ahead of the technical deep-dive, that would help us prepare questions. EOD Wednesday works for scheduling on our side.

Best,
Alice
Alice Chen
Head of Information Security | FinTrust
alice.chen@fintrust.com
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Access controls and support access — post-call recap

Hi Alice — thanks for the detailed notes. Quick responses to the asks and pointers to artifacts.

RBAC / least privilege:
- Redwood implements a role-based model layered on tenant-scoped roles. We support environment-scoped roles (prod/stage) and can map your internal roles to our policy model. Role changes are audited.

Support access / JIT:
- Primary approach: Just-in-time ephemeral sessions using short-lived tokens (OIDC/SCIM integration available).
- Approval workflow: Support session request must be tied to a ticket (we integrate with Jira/ServiceNow). For production elevates we support a two-approver policy (configurable; can require one security approver).
- All support sessions are recorded at the control plane level: who requested, approvers, duration, issued privileges, and full audit events (commands/API calls logged).

Break-glass:
- Break-glass requires a documented justification and triggers an immediate notification to your security channel. We can enforce 2 approvers for break-glass per your policy. All break-glass events are immutable and included in the audit bucket.

Audit log retention & evidence:
- Default audit retention is 13 months for activity logs; can extend per contract.
- Attaching a small redacted log extract showing a support session event and a break-glass flag (support_access_logs_stub.csv).

KMS / key handling:
- Keys are customer-scoped and managed via our KMS integration. Customers can bring your own keys (BYOK) via supported KMS/HSM providers. Access to plaintext data requires a consented operation; keys are not exportable by Redwood staff.

Artifacts we will share before the deep-dive (attached/linked):
- SOC 2 mapping (soc2_controls_mapping.xlsx)
- Support access runbook and example logs (support_access_logs_stub.csv)
- High-level access controls overview (already attached by Marissa)

Links:
- SOC2 mapping: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cRedwoodAccessControls
- Runbook: https://redwood-internal.example.com/runbooks/support-access

Let me know if you want a short demo of the ephemeral access workflow in the deep-dive. Happy to walk through a live request/approval flow.

—Rishi
